conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-21_strikes/strikes.blend, scene ST, one station per lash look (x from 62000, 40 m apart, in the order earth, ice, fire, water, lightning, metal, life, dark, poison, light, wind). Built by script (lash/tools/lash_specs.py, made from the approved DASH specs by make_lash_specs.py) from the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kit v3 and the arc strikes kit vfx_strikes_kit.fbx. No new meshes: there is no lash kit file.
conventions.made: 2026-11-21 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.strike_shape: lash: the Chain Sickle's infused strike, attack_sickle_2 (Weapons.cs:417): the weight snapped out down a lane 5.2 m long and 0.9 m wide (ChainThrow.Lane). It leaves the hand half-way through the 0.18 s windup and reaches the lane's end as the windup ends (accelerating), is held through the 0.08 s active window and whipped back over the recovery (ChainLine.cs:137-143). Every element follows the chain's curve (an easy S down the lane) and cracks at its tip.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the PLAYER's ground point (y = 0). The lane runs along lane_direction (Unity axes; the renders turn the player and lane 35 degrees toward the camera's right so the lane reads across the screen). Pieces with about_player (placement c) are laid along the lane; bodies carry their positions from the player; ribbons whose centre is "body k" are relative to that body's ground point. In game, turn the look so lane_direction is the player's facing.
conventions.chain_timing: The weight reaches distance x down the lane at t = -0.09 + 0.09 * sqrt((x - 0.4) / 4.8) s (t 0 is the end of the windup, when it reaches 5.2 m and cracks). Every streak segment is drawn as the weight passes and wiped just behind it; the crack at the tip is drawn at t 0. weight_reaches_s gives when the weight reaches each struck body. In Unity key them off the chain line itself (ChainLine.far), not a fixed delay.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body, c = along the lane from the player.
conventions.carrier: The grey stand-in chain and weight in the renders (role ref) mock the throw only: they are not in this recipe and nothing is drawn on the weapon.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies) a piece belongs to, with about_body = its position from that body (Unity axes). Written from the pass's specs (lash/tools/lash_specs.py) by lash/tools/lash_assemble_recipe.py.
conventions.per_struck_enemy: motion.per_struck_enemy = true marks a piece that exists once for each enemy the weight actually hits, placed about_body from that enemy and timed from the moment it reaches it; spawn one set per struck enemy and none on a miss. Bodies 0 to 2 are in the lane (struck_bodies); body 3 is beside it (missed_bodies) and has nothing drawn on it.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment (infused), strike_shape (lash), weapon, lash, lane_direction, chain_timing, owner, answer, look (in words), struck_bodies, missed_bodies, weight_reaches_s and per_struck_enemy_pieces.
conventions.dark_outline: Dark's hands (vfxst_hand_big_open, vfxst_hand_big_grip: one rounded organic mesh each; material st_hand_small, near-black with a violet rim) were rendered with a violet outline on their outer silhouette (Freestyle line set InkHands, colour 0.42, 0.18, 0.7 linear, thickness 1.5). Each hand is one merged mesh, so the outline never traces joins between parts. In Unity give them an outline pass in that colour on the silhouette only. The lash's shadow wisps (vfxe2_cloud_a/_b in st_sl_shadow_smoke) take the same violet silhouette outline.
conventions.poison_veins: Poison's bruise, wound, vein web and sheen are ribbons whose points were snapped onto the stand-in body's surface and sunk into it so they lie flat on the skin (the bruise shows as a flat patch about 1.5 cm proud, the fine vessels as painted lines) and ride its motion (follow_body). In Unity build them as a decal or a vein and bruise mask in the enemy's shader that spreads from the wound with the same timing; nothing should stand out of the body. Here the veins carry a sickly-green rim (st_sp_vein_rim), as the owner asked for DASH.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (ramp ones shade by facing, centre to rim), except the toon stone, which is lit toon with the ink outline. Metal uses the blue-grey st_sl_glint, Poison the sickly-rimmed st_sl_venom and st_sp_vein_rim. Metal, Light and Lightning run above the soldiers' shoulders. No stop reaches pure white: every strip frame is counted (lash/white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.revisions: 2026-11-21. Dark, picked by the owner (DASH and LASH): one OPEN hand per struck enemy rising flat-palmed out of the shadow beside it, lying 20 degrees off the floor with its palm toward the game camera so the five fingers show, held open 0.3 s, then closing on the leg and tugging. Round 1. Made from the DASH looks as approved and fixed by the owner (round 2), so every element is one family: Fire's burst is real flame, Dark one hand per struck rising from its shadow, Poison's veins rimmed sickly green, Light one clean glare.
